correctness.rationale: At n=-1 and m<d=p^r, the root-of-unity average filters the signed elementary symmetric terms of the factors d/i to degrees kt. There are at most p-1 factors of valuation one and all others have valuation at least two, so every term has valuation at least 2kt-(p-1). Congruences for all m at n=-1 therefore hold when r<=L=2t-p+1 and propagate to every integer by Pascal differences and induction on m. For r>L, write j=t-p+1 and c=[p(p-1)+q]p^(r-2) with q as in RESULT.md; t<=c<d. The factors attaining valuations one and two have the counts asserted in the proof. Minimal products in degree t use all p-1 of the former and exactly j of the latter. The normalized valuation-two product consists of p-1 complete blocks of nonzero residues followed by q extra factors. Its complete-block contribution is (1-X^(p-1))^(p-1)=1+X^(p-1) through degree p over F_p. Hence the required coefficient is 1/j! for 2<=j<=p-2, and 1 at both j=p-1 and j=p. The valuation-one normalization is a unit and all degrees >=2t have strictly larger valuation, giving exact valuation L at (n,m)=(-1,c). This is a finite difference of order d-1-c of the top-degree discrepancy, so at least one of the consecutive top-degree inputs from -1 to d-2-c fails. The degree-c valuation is not an asserted top-degree valuation.
residual_risks: Restricted to the stated prime and root-count band; no assertion for composite d or about other prime-power bands.
